title: JudgmentInference
description: Slack Message 3 (HAR-129 section 11, 12): Ghost's inference of why the human chose what they chose, and the human's verdict on that inference. The verdict and note are higher-quality supervision than the click alone. One human choice never becomes company knowledge directly: this record only feeds a candidate criterion that must be scoped and backtested.

agreement.description: agreed when the human chose Ghost's preference (the judgment is confirmed rather than contradicted), overrode otherwise; a SQL CHECK ties it to the two ids.

inferred_semantic_delta.description: What the human valued differently from Ghost, in words, plus labels from the HumanDelta vocabulary where they fit.

edit_class.description: What kind of change the human made, per class (a recipient edit is always stakeholder or recipient). A factual change labelled style would suppress learning, so the class is judged on its own (E10.3).

signal_strength.description: How much this interaction says: a click alone is at most weak; an edit is moderate; an explicit note or a corrected inference is strong (E10.4).

explicit_instructions.description: Imperative rules the human stated in a note or a correction, each with the verbatim words (E10.5). Never invented: an empty list when the human stated none.

confidence.description: How sure the inference is of its own reading, 0 to 1. Never a probability of being right about the person: it is the producer's stated certainty, calibrated later.

unknown.description: True when the inference cannot say why the human chose this: the statement then says so and no label is offered (E10.6). Unknown is a correct answer for an ambiguous choice.

evidence.description: Why Ghost inferred this (Message 3 'Why Ghost inferred this').

candidate_differences.description: How the preferred and the chosen candidate differ.

no_applicable_knowledge.description: True when no company knowledge applied; the absence is part of the evidence.

human_verdict.description: no_learning is the human's explicit opt-out (Slack "Don't learn this"): nothing is learned from this episode; no candidate criterion or knowledge is seeded from it and no later verdict changes that.

allOf.description: Every answered verdict is dated and attributed.
A correction carries the human's corrected explanation.
Nothing is corrected or dated before the human has answered.
A confirmed or no-learning inference has nothing to correct.
